mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in WORKPLACES mobility over the past four weeks reduces weekday commuter-linked retail footfall, pulling RETAIL_REC lower on a continuing basis over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days even though WORKPLACES continues to fall or stays below -40.

mechanism_narrative: A week-on-week WORKPLACES decline exceeding 20 percentage points, as observed from -16.3 to -44.3, signals a new round of movement restrictions that will suppress discretionary retail and recreation visits over the following two weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES falls more than 20 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES dropped from -16.3 to -44.3 between t-1w and t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over the next 2 weeks is equal to or higher than the prior 2-week mean despite the WORKPLACES threshold being crossed.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increase in RESIDENTIAL time-at-home and decrease in TRANSIT usage indicates a behavioral shift toward staying local, which jointly reduces cross-town retail and recreation trips over the next four weeks beyond what either series would predict alone.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL rose from 9.4 to 14.3 while TRANSIT fell from -20.6 to -26.0 in the latest week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases over the next 28 days even though RESIDENTIAL remains elevated above 12 and TRANSIT remains below -24.

mechanism_narrative: In a regime of tightening restrictions signaled by the sharp WORKPLACES drop, any rebound in PARKS visits reflects outdoor substitution rather than genuine mobility recovery, so RETAIL_REC will continue to decline over the next two weeks despite the PARKS uptick.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES below -40 while PARKS rises week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS rose from -26.4 to -19.6 while WORKPLACES fell to -44.3
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 2 weeks in tandem with the PARKS increase, indicating broad-based recovery rather than substitution.

mechanism_narrative: The snapshot falls within the Lunar New Year holiday window of mid-February 2021; holiday-driven reductions in retail footfall are temporary and will reverse once the holiday period ends, producing higher RETAIL_REC over the following four weeks relative to the holiday-depressed baseline.
evidence_refs: fact:decision date 2021-02-15 falls within the Lunar New Year period
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC remains depressed or continues to fall for more than one week after the holiday period ends.

mechanism_narrative: Stable elevated GROCERY_PHARM mobility alongside falling RETAIL_REC indicates households are substituting essential shopping trips for discretionary retail visits; this divergence is expected to persist, keeping RETAIL_REC suppressed over the next week.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM stayed near 30 while RETAIL_REC fell to -28.9
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rebounds within the next week while GROCERY_PHARM remains flat, breaking the hypothesized substitution link.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in PARKS mobility above -20 signals growing comfort with outdoor activity that will spill over into retail and recreation visits once restrictions ease, lifting RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises above -20 for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS rose from -26.4 to -19.6 in latest week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC continues to decline over the next 28 days despite PARKS remaining above -20.

mechanism_narrative: Joint deterioration in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT indicates a coordinated policy-driven restriction on movement; when both fall together, RETAIL_REC is pulled down more strongly over the next two weeks than either series alone would suggest.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES fell to -44.3 and TRANSIT fell to -26.0 in the same week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC stabilizes or rises over the next 2 weeks even as both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT remain depressed.
